4.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.762 of 2019, under Sections 363, 323, 376D IPC and Section 3/4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act, 2012, Police Station Hapur Nagar, District Hapur with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have fleeced and fooled the daughter of the informant on 10.11.2019 and sent her alongwith co-accused person Raja on his scooty whereby who had taken the victim to Modinagar and from where the applicant is stated to have taken her all the way to Agra and has committed rape with her and from Agra, the applicant is stated to have taken the victim to Aligarh and is stated to have even ravished her in the presence of his wife and is stated to have beaten her.
On hearing her shrieks, the persons of the locality are stated to have taken the applicant and the victim to the police station whereby she was retrieved.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The victim is a consenting party as she had gone with the applicant all the way to Agra then to Aligarh and has not raised any alarm.
The prosecution story is filled up with embellishments, as such the applicant is entitled for bail.
There is nothing on record to suggest that the applicant is minor.
The said age has been shown after legal consultation.
Learned counsel has further stated that not even any ossification test of the victim has been conducted as it is an admitted fact that she had not gone to school.
There is nothing on record to corroborate the prosecution story of the age of the victim.
It has to be ascertained at least via ossification test.
Learned counsel has further stated that the charge in the case was framed on 24.02.2020 and since then, only two prosecution witnesses have been examined including the victim.

More than three years have passed for the incarceration of the applicant and there is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial as his Fundamental Rights enshrined in Article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 12.12.2019.
7. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the age of the victim at the time of offence was 14 years only, as such she was not in a condition to grant consent.
The fundamental elements of willingness and consent are absent.

Learned A.G.A. has further stated that even during her examination in court,
the victim has stated her age to be 16 years which has been taken up about two years Raju @ Ashok vs State Of Up Others on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136783620/
2 after the incident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus even if she is considered to be a consenting party, her consent pails into insignificance and can't be taken to have been granted.
The applicant is a married person and has subjected a teen aged girl to his lust and is not entitled for bail.

8. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the evidence on record, and also taking into consideration the said fact of the applicant being a married person and despite the fact he has committed the offence and the victim being a girl of 14 years of age, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
9. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

10. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, preferably within a period of one year from the date of production of a certified copy of this order or as early as possible in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that as a new ground the applicant is entitled for bail as the applicant is incarcerated in jail since 12.12.2019 and more than five years have passed since then.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

7. The status report of the trial was called from the court concerned and as per the report dated 30.11.2024, in all six witnesses have been examined to date and only the statement of the Investigating Officers Avinash Gautam and Subodh Saxena remains to be examined.

8. After hearing learned counsels for the parties and taking into consideration that the victim has sustained several injuries on her body parts, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
9. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

10. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
